zeros off the line”. That is contrary to the idea behind Principle 12.1: random
unitary polynomials can have large zero gaps — conjecturally with the same
size and frequency as the ζ-function — which influence the nearby gaps but
do not destroy the fact that the polynomial is unitary.

unit_result_entry.why_material: Separates asymptotically false causal stories from finite-height algorithms that successfully locate records, while showing why truncated initial terms cannot capture the true extreme scale.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A false asymptotic explanation can remain an effective finite-height search heuristic: local large gaps and biased early Riemann-Siegel terms locate records even though neither can supply the true extreme scale.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: At current heights, record values associated with large gaps can outgrow known Omega benchmarks despite being lower-order asymptotically. Filters based on initial Riemann-Siegel terms have found large values efficiently, but a truncation as short as sqrt(log t) has a deterministic size ceiling and cannot approximate the conjectured largest values; the long tail can dominate through small aggregate bias.
directed.conceptual_reading: Discovery utility and explanatory truth are different signals. A cheap proxy may enrich a search region without preserving the mechanism or scale of the target phenomenon.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Truncated Riemann-Siegel sums serve as computational filters, while the full tail and carrier-wave decomposition expose what the proxy forgets.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Success in the accessible range does not validate the causal story or extrapolate to carrier-dominated heights. The source leaves truly asymptotic location heuristics open.
directed.uncertainty: The truncated-sum display has layout risk, but its size limitation, historical filtering success, and asymptotic caveat are prose-supported.
